review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the SL2 group-element definitions and lemmas (unipotent, lowerUnipotent, dualMatrix, diagonalTorus) in the RestrictedTilting directory. I checked how the other files that use standardBasis and the unipotent lemmas treat their simp attributes. I checked the imports of WeightBounds and CharacterExpansions to see where unipotent_zero is defined. I could not confirm whether XChartLineEval and StandardLifts are ever imported together, so the duplicate-lemma point is stated conditionally. I did not run Lean, so nothing here claims an observed simp failure or loop. Both findings are about missing or inconsistent simp-set coverage. findings.excerpt: @[simp] lemma unipotent_inv (t : k) : (unipotent k t)⁻¹ = unipotent k (-t) := by
findings.problem: The simp interface for the two root-group families is asymmetric. For lowerUnipotent, both `lowerUnipotent_zero` and `lowerUnipotent_inv` are @[simp]. For unipotent, `unipotent_zero` is not @[simp], and `unipotent_inv` is only made simp here, in a late file, instead of next to its siblings. So the normal form `unipotent k 0 = 1` is not reached by simp, even though the simp lemma `unipotent_inv` can produce `unipotent k (-0)`. Proving `unipotent_inv` itself has to name `unipotent_zero` by hand (`simp only [add_neg_cancel, unipotent_zero]`). Other proofs pass it explicitly too, e.g. `simpa [unipotent_zero] using hc' 0` in WeightBounds. A non-simp duplicate `unipotent_inverse` with the same statement exists in XChartLineEval, so the same rewrite is split across two names, only one of them simp.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `unipotent_zero` as @[simp] where it is defined in SL2Definitions.lean, to match `lowerUnipotent_zero`. Move `unipotent_inv` (keeping @[simp]) next to `unipotent_add`, in the same style as `lowerUnipotent_inv` in WeightBounds. If XChartLineEval is or can be imported after that point, replace `unipotent_inverse` by it. The orientation is fine: it pushes inversion into the parameter and always terminates.
findings.benefit: The upper and lower unipotent families get the same simp behaviour. Goals containing `(unipotent k t)⁻¹` or `unipotent k 0` normalise without hand-supplied lemmas. The duplicated statement (`unipotent_inverse`, `unipotent_inv`) is removed, so later files do not have to choose between a simp and a non-simp version.

findings.excerpt: (standardBasis k n).constr k (fun i => c i)
findings.problem: `standardBasis` and `highestCoefficientMap` are plain defs with no evaluation lemmas. `standardBasis` is defined as `(binaryBasis k n).dualBasis`, and `highestCoefficientMap` as a `Basis.constr`. The only way to compute with them is to unfold the definitions inside simp sets. `highestCoefficientMap_lower_orbit` ends with `simp [highestCoefficientMap]`. `standardHighest_lower_orbit` and `standardBasis_weight` unfold `standardBasis` to reach `Module.Basis.dualBasis_apply_self`, as in `simp only [..., standardBasis, LinearMap.sum_apply, ...]`. SteinbergDuality and SimpleModules do `change ... standardBasis k n ...` in several places. This exposes the representation of the definitions, which unfold to `dualBasis` and `constr`, and ties every caller to it. The canonical normal forms, `highestCoefficientMap k n c (standardBasis k n i) = c i` and `standardBasis k n i (binaryBasis k n j) = if j = i then 1 else 0`, are not available to `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma highestCoefficientMap_standardBasis ... : highestCoefficientMap k n c (standardBasis k n i) = c i`, proved from `Module.Basis.constr_basis`. Add `@[simp] lemma standardBasis_apply_binaryBasis (i j : Fin (n+1)) : standardBasis k n i (binaryBasis k n j) = if j = i then 1 else 0`, proved from `Module.Basis.dualBasis_apply_self`. Then `highestCoefficientMap_lower_orbit` can use `simp` after `map_sum`/`map_smul`. The `standardBasis` unfolding in `standardHighest_lower_orbit` and `standardBasis_weight` can also be dropped, and downstream `change` steps replaced by rewrites.
findings.benefit: Callers no longer unfold `standardBasis` and `highestCoefficientMap` to their `dualBasis`/`constr` definitions. Simp reaches the intended normal form (`c i`, an indicator) directly. Later files such as SteinbergDuality and SimpleModules also get these lemmas.
